mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has been flattening over the last four weeks (-17.3, -17.3, -17.6, -16.0), showing a mild upward drift. This autocorrelated momentum should persist, producing a modestly higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -17.6 to -16.0 in the latest week
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the observed upward drift, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES fell sharply in the latest week (-13.7 to -20.0), consistent with stricter enforcement of the England-wide lockdown that began 5 Nov. Such a sharp tightening in workplace mobility typically precedes a lagged suppression of discretionary retail trips as enforcement broadens to non-essential retail.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -13.7 to -20.0 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline further over the following two weeks despite the WORKPLACES drop exceeding the 5-point threshold, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL (14.4 to 14.9) combined with persistently depressed TRANSIT (around -27) indicates intensifying stay-at-home behavior. When both series move in this reinforcing direction simultaneously, households further reduce non-essential outings, compounding suppression of RETAIL_REC beyond what either series would predict alone.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose each of the last three weeks while TRANSIT stayed below -26
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise and TRANSIT remaining depressed, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: With the lockdown scheduled to end around 2 Dec and Christmas shopping season approaching, consumer anticipation of reopening plus pent-up holiday retail demand should produce a rebound in RETAIL_REC within the four-week window, even while restrictions are formally in place during part of it.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-11-15 falls roughly two weeks before scheduled lockdown easing on 2 Dec 2020
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean remains at or below its 28-day backward mean despite the approaching lockdown end and holiday season, the seasonal rebound hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been highly volatile (-13.1, -17.3, -23.7, -15.9), likely reflecting weather-driven substitution between outdoor and indoor/retail activity. A sharp rebound in PARKS above a threshold signals that outdoor substitution is drawing trips away from shopping destinations, temporarily depressing RETAIL_REC the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 7 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -23.7 to -15.9 in the latest week, a rise of 7.8 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a PARKS rise exceeding 7 points, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under the current national lockdown regime, non-essential retail is legally closed, capping RETAIL_REC's ability to recover regardless of underlying demand signals. As long as this regime holds, RETAIL_REC should remain flat or slightly negative, only shifting materially once restrictions are lifted.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC both remain deeply negative across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises substantially (more than 3 points) over the next two weeks while the lockdown remains formally in force, the policy-cap hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained consistently positive and stable (1.4 to 3.7) across the snapshot, indicating essential shopping trips are the dominant and steady component of the broader retail category. This stability implies RETAIL_REC will show only minor short-term fluctuation in the immediate next week, absent new shocks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive and rose modestly each week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC moves by more than 3 points in either direction in the next week while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable, the stability hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES (-13.7 to -20.0) and persistently low TRANSIT (around -27) jointly indicate a broad contraction in overall out-of-home economic activity. When both commuting-linked series fall together, the combined reduction in trip-chaining opportunities compounds to suppress RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points while TRANSIT remains below -25
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped 6.3 points while TRANSIT stayed near -27.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks despite both WORKPLACES dropping more than 5 points and TRANSIT remaining below -25, the joint-contraction hypothesis is rejected.
